repos.readme: Large Scale Social Media Sentiment and Trend Analytics Using MongoDB A university Big Data Analytics project. It loads 2,944,814 real tweets into MongoDB, cleans them, adds sentiment, topics and keywords with lightweight NLP, pre aggregates them with MongoDB aggregation pipelines, serves the results through a FastAPI REST API, and shows them in a React dashboard. Performance experiments measure ingestion, indexing, aggregation and NLP at 100K, 500K, 1M and 2.95M documents. The core platform runs on one machine with 16 GB of RAM and no GPU: data is processed in batches by Python and MongoDB. A Big Data Lab extension adds the distributed side: an Apache Spark pipeline that builds a bronze / silver / gold Parquet data lake, and a 3 shard MongoDB cluster that compares shard keys. Its results, architecture and course concepts (5 Vs, CAP, Hadoop mapping) are shown in tabs on the dashboard's Big Data Lab page; see docs/bigdata.md. More screenshots (sentiment, trends, topics, anomalies, explorer, performance, dark mode) are in docs/images. What is in it The data, honestly Posts are real. FiveThirtyEight's russian troll tweets dataset: tweets from accounts that Twitter identified as linked to the Internet Research Agency, collected by Linvill and Warren at Clemson University, published under CC BY 4.0. 2,946,207 rows were read; 2,944,814 were stored after removing 1,392 duplicate tweet ids and 1 empty tweet. Dates run from 2012 to 2018. It is not a sample of ordinary Twitter users. Every account is a state linked troll account, so the results describe that campaign, not public opinion. Engagement is synthetic. The dataset has no like, reply or retweet counts. To exercise the engagement module, scripts/synthesize engagement.py generates them from each author's real follower count. Every such value is stored with engagement.synthetic true and every engagement chart in the dashboard carries a Synthetic data badge. Do not draw conclusions about real audiences from them. Sentiment is a model prediction, English only. The classifier was trained and evaluated on TweetEval (test macro F1 0.58, see docs/performance.md). It has not been evaluated on the IRA tweets themselves, which carry no sentiment labels. Non English posts are counted as not analyzed . Location is the account level region field from the source (country only), known for 80.6% of posts. Details: docs/dataset.

repos.readme: AgentForge A multi agent AI research assistant that shows its sources and its failures . You ask a question; three CrewAI agents work in sequence and return a sourced report. Project site: Stack: React + Vite + TypeScript (frontend), Python + FastAPI + CrewAI (backend), GitHub Pages (project site). Status: built and tested as described under Testing. It has not yet been run against a live LLM or deployed as a hosted app. See Limitations. Screenshots Both screenshots were captured against a stubbed backend (a test harness), so the report text is placeholder output, not model output. Why it is built this way Sources are never written by the model. The sources list in the API response is recorded by the search and fetch tools from real network activity. Each source is labelled "page read" or "search result only". Progress is real. The timeline and agent cards are driven by events emitted from the running crew (task callbacks and tool calls). Nothing is simulated. Failures are never reported as success. Model errors, timeouts, and missing sources (when required) end the job as failed with a reason. The UI never substitutes sample results. Async jobs. Research takes minutes, so POST returns 202 with a job id and the UI polls. This avoids proxy timeouts on free hosts. fetch page only accepts public http(s) addresses (basic SSRF guard). Run locally Requirements: Python 3.10+, Node 20+, Git, and one model (see below). Quick path: scripts/setup.sh , edit backend/.env , then scripts/dev.sh (macOS/Linux/Git Bash). On Windows use scripts\setup.ps1 and scripts\dev.ps1 . Manual steps: The header should read "Backend connected" next to your model name. Choosing a model Model choice is configuration only. Free tiers and quotas change, so check each provider's current terms. Small local models can struggle with structured output. When that happens the report is shown as raw text with a visible structured output failed check. Configuration API Jobs are held in server memory (last 50) and are lost on restart. repos.readme: Enterprise Agentic RAG Orchestrator Developed by: Sahaj S. GitHub: @SahajIVVIX 1 Enterprise Agentic RAG Orchestrator is a production grade Multi Agent Agentic RAG system designed for complex enterprise workflows. A Supervisor→Worker→Validator pipeline routes every query to the right specialist agent, with a LangGraph powered Corrective RAG loop for high fidelity retrieval and a strict human in the loop protocol for external actions. Resume & Portfolio Highlights Multi Agent Orchestration : Designed a stateful Supervisor Worker Validator architecture utilizing LangGraph and LangChain to route queries among specialized agents (Corrective RAG, Natural Language to SQL, Human in the Loop external tools, and Conversational agents). Corrective RAG (CRAG) with LangGraph : Implemented a self correcting retrieval graph that uses an LLM grader to evaluate document relevance, dynamically triggering query rewriting and re retrieval (bounded to 2 iterations to prevent latency spikes). Hybrid Retrieval & Hierarchical Context Expansion : Integrated 384 dimensional dense semantic vectors (Qdrant) and sparse keyword search (BM25) with CrossEncoder neural reranking ( ms marco MiniLM L 6 v2 ) and parent child chunk expansion (200 token retrieval units expanded to 800 token parent context). RAGAS Quality Benchmarking : Achieved 0.81 Faithfulness , 1.00 Context Precision , 0.90 Context Recall , and 0.75 Answer Relevancy across enterprise evaluation datasets. Enterprise Security & Safeguards : Engineered a defense in depth security perimeter with constant time two tier API key authentication, IP based sliding window rate limiting via Redis, regex based prompt injection barriers, read only SQLite/MySQL URI isolation, and symmetric Fernet encryption at rest for external credentials. Human in the Loop Protocol : Implemented a strict Draft → Confirm → Execute workflow for transactional operations (email actions) with domain allow listing and hourly rate caps. High Performance Caching : Designed an Approximate Nearest Neighbor (ANN) semantic cache using Qdrant (cosine similarity ≥ 0.96) to deliver sub millisecond responses on repeated semantic queries, backed by Redis for multi tenant conversation session persistence. repos.description: Intelligent data cleaning system using Reinforcement Learning and LLMs (OpenEnv) to optimize datasets with context-aware decisions.
repos.readme: 🧹 OpenEnv Data Cleaning RL Agent Reinforcement Learning meets Large Language Models for Autonomous Data Cleaning An agent that doesn't just clean data — it learns how to clean it. 🚀 Live Demo · 📖 Documentation · ⚡ Quick Start "Traditional pipelines tell the agent what to do. This system lets the agent figure it out." 🧠 The Core Idea Most data cleaning pipelines are static rule engines : hardcoded if null → fill with mean , if duplicate → drop . They're brittle, opinionated, and blind to context. This project takes a completely different approach. Instead of rules, it uses a reward signal . The agent observes a dataset, chooses a cleaning action, receives feedback from the environment, and adapts. The behavior isn't programmed — it emerges from what gets rewarded. This is the intersection of two powerful ideas: The LLM provides reasoning and language understanding . The RL environment provides structured feedback and ground truth . Together, they form an agent that can handle messy, real world tabular data without being told exactly what to do. 🏗️ Architecture How a single step works 📦 Project Structure ⚙️ The RL Environment (OpenEnv) The custom environment is the heart of this project. It's designed around three principles: 1. Observations are informative, not overwhelming Rather than dumping the full dataset at every step, the environment sends a structured summary — missing value counts, duplicate counts, and a small data sample for context. This mirrors how a real analyst would assess a dataset at a glance. 2. Rewards are shaped carefully 3. The anti loop system is non negotiable One of the hardest problems in RL agent design is the agent getting stuck in a reward neutral cycle. This system tracks action history and applies an exponentially increasing penalty if the same action is selected consecutively — forcing the agent to explore or terminate. 🤖 The LLM Agent The agent uses Llama 3 via OpenRouter as its reasoning engine. At each step, the agent receives a formatted prompt containing: The current observation (state) The full action space A brief history of recent actions and rewards An instruction to reason before selecting This is a zero shot, context window driven decision loop — no fine tuning required. repos.readme: Deep DCGAN Reproducibility Study: Architecture & Analytics A research centric implementation of the DCGAN paper (Radford et al., 2015), modernized with 2018 2022 stability techniques and a professional post training analytics pipeline. 🚀 The Vision This project isn't just about training another GAN—it's about understanding it. While most implementations just show you a grid of fuzzy images, this study dives deep into the "black box" of the Generator and Discriminator to visualize exactly how latent vectors become features. Key Highlights Modern Stability : Upgraded the 2015 baseline with LSGAN (Least Squares) and Spectral Normalization to prevent the dreaded "vanishing gradient" problem. Deep Diagnostics : A custom GANAnalyzer class that hooks into the model's internal layers to visualize learned filters and feature maps without needing to retrain. High Fidelity Evaluation : Automated 4 panel dashboarding for immediate assessments of model convergence and Nash Equilibrium. DCGAN Reproducibility Study: Paper vs. Modern Implementation A formal comparison between the baseline architecture proposed by Radford et al. (2015) and this enhanced, high stability version for facial/object generation. Executive Summary While this project replicates the All Convolutional architecture and upsampling strategy defined in the 2015 paper, it adopts several modern training paradigms discovered between 2017 and 2020. This implementation introduces a dedicated GANAnalyzer framework that mirrors paper's Figure 5 but expands it with professional metrics.
